summary: Kenshi Kusano specializes in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Otani University from circa 1971 to 1980 and served there as a professor from circa 1998 to 2018.

Kenta Suzuki works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1994–1998) and Kyoto University (~1999–2007), and was an associate professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College circa 2011.

Kenyu Mitomo is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Rissho University, UC Berkeley, and under teachers including Akira Hirakawa. He served as Dean of Buddhist Studies at Rissho University (1968–2015).

Kevin Alan Vose specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned degrees from Bates College and the University of Virginia, studying under doctoral supervisor Jeffrey Hopkins and traditional teacher Khen Rinpoche Ngawang Jinpa.
Kevin Buckelew works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Sarah Lawrence College, with doctoral supervision from Chün-fang Yü, Bernard Faure, and Zhaohua Yang.
Khakyab Dorje was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye (~1886–1899) and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo (~1886–1892).
Kham Sum Zilnön Gyepa Dorjé studied under Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso and Khenpo Shenga, and later taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Khammai Dhammasami is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his DPhil at the University of Oxford (~1999–2004). He served as Oxford Buddhist chaplain, founded Oxford Buddha Vihara and Shan State Buddhist University, and taught at ITBMU.
Khangsar Tenpe Wangchuk was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teachers Jampel Gyepai Dorje and Lodro Gyatso.
Khen Gen Jampal Dorjé studied under Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso and Khenpo Shenga.
Khen Rinpoche Ngawang Jinpa specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Drepung Loseling Monastery and served as a professor at St. Joseph's College, Darjeeling (attested 1995).
Khenchen Ngawang Khyen Rab Gyatso studied under Dilgo Khyentse and Trulshik Rinpoche.

Khenchen Palden Sherab Rinpoche worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Gochen and Riwoche monasteries and under Dudjom Rinpoche, later chairing the Nyingma section at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1967–1984).
Khenchen Tashi Özer studied under teachers including Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Thegchog Dorje, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy scholar. He studied under Khenpo Gangshar and the 16th Karmapa, and served as abbot of Rumtek Monastery (~1968–1981) and Gampo Abbey (~1984–2023).
Khenchen Tsewang Rigdzin studied under Shechen Gyaltsab, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Khenpo Shenga.
Khenpo Appey was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Dzongsar Monastery and under Drakgyab Lodrö, and served as director of Sakya College from 1972 to 1985.

Khenpo Dazer specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima and held teaching posts at Shri Singha Shedra and Ngagyur Nyingma Institute.
Khenpo Gangshar was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Shechen Monastery under teachers including Khyentse Ozer, later serving as a senior teacher at Shechen Monastery.
Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima and Khenchen Dazer (~1951–1957), among other traditional teachers.
